title: Why El Terrerazo tastes the way it does

lede.text: The temperature swing in this vineyard gives the wine its typical colour. It also sets how well its acidity is balanced.

chapters.title: A vineyard in Utiel
paras: El Terrerazo's vineyard lies in the municipality of Utiel, in Valencia. It has a protected designation of origin of its own.
It was recognised as a vino de pago on 17 September 2010.

chapters.title: Sun all day, slow ripening
paras: The land here barely falls away, so the vineyard is in sunlight for the whole day. Together with the altitude of 870 m, this gives a very high heat sum. In other words, days and nights differ a lot in temperature. The grapes ripen very slowly as a result.

chapters.title: Limy sandy loam
paras: The soil is a sandy loam. It is limy, with a basic pH. The wine owes its finesse to this soil.

chapters.title: A red from four main grapes
paras: El Terrerazo makes a red wine. Four grapes lead. Bobal and Syrah are two of them. Merlot and Garnacha Tinta are the other two.
A red can also be made from Bobal alone. Cabernet Sauvignon is allowed as a secondary grape. So is Tempranillo, also called Cencibel or Tinto de Toro.
